decisions.question: Change (b): which signature makes a value of the wrong type a compile error without changing any fixture outside bus-api@v1? The orchestrator named publish<T, V extends T>(MultiWriterTopic<T> topic, V value).

options.label: publish<T, V extends T>, as named
options.consequence: Rejects a wrong value type with could_not_infer, but a state topic passed to publish now leaves T uninferred (dynamic) and the analyzer adds inference_failure_on_function_invocation under strict-inference; navigation-api@v1's reject/current_route_is_claimed_by_the_executor.dart then fails on lines 10 and 12, so a fixture outside bus-api@v1 would have to change: a run-stop-candidate under this step's rule (experiment T10, probe P2 line 27).

options.label: publish<T extends Object?, V extends T>
options.consequence: The same type relation (Object? is an unbounded parameter's bound already); only a failed inference falls back to Object? instead of dynamic, so a state topic reports argument_type_not_assignable alone. Wrong value types are rejected identically (could_not_infer); every fixture outside bus-api@v1 passes unchanged (T3, T7).

options.label: keep publish<T>(MultiWriterTopic<T>, T) and drop (b)
options.consequence: No fixture changes, but Spec §4.2's compile-time typing stays unmet: publish(EventTopic<int>, 'one') and a DeepLink to nav.resolved-intent compile and fail at run time (navigation-api@v1 Refinement 9).

decisions.chosen: publish<T extends Object?, V extends T>
decisions.why: It meets (b)'s purpose exactly and is the only one of the three that satisfies both (b) and the step's compatibility rule. The prescribed spelling differs only in the implicit bound, and that difference is what produces the extra strict-inference warning. Found by experiment, not by the orchestrator's search for explicit type arguments, which was correct as far as it went (only bus-api@v1's own surface/bus.dart and no_publisherless_state_publish.dart pass explicit type arguments) but missed that a reject fixture pins the full diagnostic set of a line. Signal that would have changed my mind: a lint in package:lints/recommended flagging the redundant bound (T0 shows none fires) or the orchestrator treating the spelled-out bound as a different change from the one it authorized, in which case the named form is a run-stop-candidate with the T10 evidence.

decisions.question: Does G22 pin that the publishes a connection causes are made from a provider-zone microtask, never within activate, as S12 asked, or keep only 'delivered once the microtasks queued during activate have run'?

options.label: pin the deferral, with a case
options.consequence: A runtime that delivers connection outputs inside activate fails; a topology activated right after another (in a module acquire, or a bootstrap) receives the first one's connection outputs.

options.label: leave the earlier wording
options.consequence: Admits a runtime that delivers connection outputs synchronously inside activate, which the earlier wording also satisfied literally.

decisions.chosen: pin the deferral, with a case
decisions.why: Seeded defect T10 (connection publishes made within activate) fails the new G22 case and the existing 'G34 ... the order of the activations before start does not change what is delivered' case, so the deferral is what makes activation order irrelevant; the navigation-api-fixtures runtime already behaves this way and every consumer suite passes on it.

decisions.question: How do the new (a) cases detect a late connection?

options.label: a withLatestFrom gate over a state read
options.consequence: Drops a primary value that arrives before the read's first value, so a late connection shows as a missing output; the same shape as navigation-api@v1's nav-resolver, so the cases model the deep-link bootstrap.

options.label: a combineLatest or a recorder-order check
options.consequence: combineLatest emits late rather than dropping, which a flush hides; an order check over envelopes cannot see when a read received its first value, since the connection is not a publish.

decisions.chosen: a withLatestFrom gate over a state read
decisions.why: It turns the timing question into a value difference the harness can assert synchronously, and S12's connection probe already showed it separates the S11 runtime from a correct one.

decisions.question: Change (b): extend G11 and G19 with the value-type rule, or add a guarantee?

options.label: extend G11 and G19
options.consequence: No new id, but one rule stated twice and the reject lines split across two files whose guarantees are about the topic variant, not the value.

decisions.chosen: new G40 with its own reject library
decisions.why: The value-type rule is distinct from the variant rule G11 and G19 state; a separate id lets phase gates restrict by it. Every reject code was confirmed (T3, T4).

decisions.question: Explicit type arguments can still widen T through Dart's covariant generics (publish<num, double> on an EventTopic<int> compiles, probe P16, P26). What does G40 say about them?

options.label: state the limit in G40
options.consequence: The guarantee is exact about what it covers (inferred type arguments); no runtime behavior is promised for the widened call.

options.label: add a run-time guarantee (a throw) with a behavior case
options.consequence: Closes the hole at run time, but adds a check on every publish path and a rule no consumer asked for.

options.label: say nothing
options.consequence: G40 would read as if every wrong value were a compile error, which is false.

A static check (nidana-checks@v1) is the cheaper closure if it ever matters. Signal that would change it: a consumer contract or app pattern that forwards topics through explicitly widened generics.

decisions.question: After the connection, does every later delivery reach a topology's read during that delivery, so the deliveries start() makes reach a topology's reads in queue order across topics? The navigation-api-fixtures runtime, which S12 offered as making (a) hold, connects synchronously but holds back the deliveries made before the RxDart replay's first microtask, so a state publish queued between two queued events reaches a withLatestFrom read after the second event (T10: [41, 51] where [41, 57] is the queue order).

options.label: pin it: a connected read receives each later delivery during that delivery
options.consequence: A restored state queued before start (an auth session written by a service) reaches the nav-resolver's read before a deep link queued after it; the runtime needs a synchronous, non-replaying path for topology reads (the stand-in uses a sync broadcast controller per cell); every consumer suite passes on it (T7). Goes beyond Spec §3.3's general position that cross-topic ordering is not guaranteed, for synchronous deliveries on one bus.

options.label: pin only that the connection precedes the queue
options.consequence: What S12 asked for literally; the navigation-api-fixtures runtime suffices, but a queued state publish can reach a topology after a later-queued event, so the deep-link guard can see the initial auth state instead of the restored one.

decisions.chosen: pin it: a connected read receives each later delivery during that delivery
decisions.why: The delivery rule already says a delivery runs synchronously and hands the envelope to the subscriptions, and G34 says start() delivers the queue in order; a read the connection reached is an established subscriber, and only RxDart's replay buffering made the window. Spec §3.13 makes the barrier the deep-link mechanism, which only works if the queue reaches the resolver in order. Medium confidence because it strengthens cross-topic ordering at a topology beyond Spec §3.3's portable minimum. Signal that would change it: nidana.runtime's design finding that a non-replaying read path costs more than the guarantee is worth, or the owner preferring Spec §3.3's weaker stance for portability.

notes_for_orchestrator: Compatibility verification: the orchestrator's search for explicit type arguments was correct (only bus-api@v1's own surface/bus.dart and reject/no_publisherless_state_publish.dart pass them; both changed here), but it was not the only way (b) breaks a fixture. The named form publish<T, V extends T> leaves T uninferred for a state topic, and strict-inference adds inference_failure_on_function_invocation on lines 10 and 12 of navigation-api@v1's reject/current_route_is_claimed_by_the_executor.dart, which fails its exact (line, code) match (experiment T10). The contract therefore declares publish<T extends Object?, V extends T>, the same type relation with the bound written out, under which every fixture outside bus-api@v1 passes unchanged. If the orchestrator reads the bound as a different change from the one it authorized, the named form is a run-stop-candidate (breaking amendment of navigation-api@v1's fixture) with T10 as evidence. The real package must keep the bound: a phase that simplifies it fails navigation-api@v1's gate.

(a) goes one clause beyond S12's request (decision at 19:42:48Z, would_have_asked): a read the connection reached receives each later delivery during that delivery, so start()'s queue reaches a topology's reads in queue order across topics. The navigation-api-fixtures runtime does not meet this (a queued state publish reaches a withLatestFrom read after a later-queued event); this experiment's stand-in does, with topology reads on a synchronous broadcast controller per cell instead of the RxDart subject. nidana.runtime's design must give topology reads a non-replaying synchronous path, emit the connection from the subject's current value or buffer before activate returns, and defer the publishes the connection causes to a provider-zone microtask; observed subscriptions keep G17's microtask first delivery.

S14 (flutter-binding@v1), bootstrap order after (a): the bootstrap may activate the APPLICATION topologies (the nav-resolver), construct the NavigationExecutor and call bus.start() in one synchronous block with no pump or microtask between; a deep link queued before start(), even before the resolver's activation, is resolved and guarded, and a state written before start() (a restored session) reaches the resolver before any event queued after it. What (a) does not change: NavigationExecutor reads router.stack at construction (S12 note 4), so the Navigator must be mounted, or the router must accept calls before mount, before the executor is constructed, and start() follows that; connection-caused publishes and observed first values still wait for a provider-zone microtask, which under testWidgets on a production-provider bus runs on the next pump, so widgets take their first frame from getCurrentValue (G17). S12's observation that pumpWidget hid the gap no longer matters for correctness. The widget-test recorder attaches before start() and records in attachment order before observers (delivery rule, (d)).

navigation-api@v1 can now take compatible, editorial follow-ups (not made here): (1) a G1 reject line on nav.resolved-intent, pages.publish(NavigationTopics.resolvedIntent, DeepLink(uri)), which reports could_not_infer alone (probe P19); (2) Refinement 8 can cite bus-api@v1 G22 and G34 directly and drop 'bus-api@v1's fixtures do not pin it', and G24's 'as Refinement 8 reads them'; (3) Refinement 9 can cite bus-api@v1 G40; (4) its Validation sentence about the patched runtime can point at docs/auto-run/experiments/bus-api-amendment/.
